dynamodb_add_gsi: MiniStack's CreationDateTime has one-second resolution: a table deleted and recreated within the same second keeps an identical CreationDateTime (verified). TableId does change on recreation (verified), so table_not_recreated compares TableId and CreationDateTime.

MiniStack makes a new GSI ACTIVE immediately; real AWS backfills for minutes (CREATING). An agent that never waits for ACTIVE passes here but could finish before the index is usable on AWS. The grader reads the status at grading time.
The index's ItemCount reads 0 in MiniStack right after backfill (it is a periodically refreshed statistic on AWS too), so it is not asserted.
iam_least_privilege: IAM policies are stored but never evaluated by MiniStack, and no Lambda runs under the role, so least privilege is checked statically (grader/policy.py) against IAM semantics.

MiniStack accepts CreateRole with a malformed trust policy (verified: "{bad" is stored); real AWS rejects it with MalformedPolicyDocument. The grader parses the trust policy and fails if it is not valid JSON.

Deliberate allowances, so standard Lambda practice is not a false fail: logs:CreateLogGroup, logs:CreateLogStream and logs:PutLogEvents are accepted on any resource including "*" (exactly AWS's AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole); dynamodb:UpdateItem and BatchWriteItem are accepted alongside PutItem on the table ARN ("writes items"); s3:ListBucket on the bucket is accepted only with an s3:prefix condition limited to reports/. Everything else, any wildcard action (incl. "s3:Get*") and any non-logs Resource "*", fails.
The grader finds the role by its trust policy (the prompt names no role); exactly one role trusting lambda.amazonaws.com must exist. Permissions boundaries and SCPs are not considered.
s3_lifecycle_add_rule: "Lifecycle rules are stored but not automatically executed" (parity.json). Graded statically from the stored configuration; objects are never observed expiring.

MiniStack drops the legacy top-level rule "Prefix" (deprecated in favour of Filter.Prefix): a rule PUT with Prefix "tmp/" reads back as Filter {} (whole bucket). Real AWS keeps the prefix. An agent using the legacy form is graded on the widened rule MiniStack stored and fails the tmp/ assertion, though the same call would be correct on real AWS. Known potential false fail.
s3_logs_bucket: MiniStack accepts PutBucketVersioning with any Status (verified: "Disabled", "banana") and returns it from GetBucketVersioning. Real AWS only accepts Enabled|Suspended (MalformedXML otherwise). The grader therefore fails any stored Status other than never-set/Suspended, because that state is unreachable on AWS and the agent's call would have errored there.

MiniStack does not apply AWS's default Block Public Access to new buckets: GetPublicAccessBlock on a fresh bucket returns NoSuchPublicAccessBlockConfiguration, while real AWS (since April 2023) returns all four flags true. The grader requires an explicit, readable all-true configuration, so an agent that relies on the AWS default fails here but would pass the same grader on real AWS. Known potential false fail; not hidden.
"Lifecycle rules are stored but not automatically executed" (parity.json). Graded statically from the stored configuration; object expiry itself is never observed.
s3_notification_add: MiniStack delivers S3 event notifications to a queue whose policy does not allow s3.amazonaws.com to SendMessage, and accepts PutBucketNotificationConfiguration for such a queue (it only checks the queue exists). Real AWS rejects that PUT ("Unable to validate the following destination configurations"). The grader therefore also checks thumbnails-q's policy statically (thumbnails_policy_allows_s3), so a passing behavioural check alone is not enough.

MiniStack sends s3:TestEvent messages to the queues when the configuration is written (as AWS does). Behavioural checks look for a grader-generated unique object key, so test events and messages the agent produced do not cause false passes.
s3_policy_add_statement: "Bucket policies are stored but not evaluated" (parity.json). Whether plain-HTTP requests are actually rejected cannot be observed, so the Deny is checked statically against IAM semantics (grader/policy.py).

MiniStack accepts PutBucketPolicy with invalid JSON and with Resources that name a different bucket (verified); real AWS rejects both with MalformedPolicy. The grader fails such policies (policy_valid_for_bucket) instead of trusting that the PUT succeeded.
sns_sqs_fanout: MiniStack delivers SNS messages to an SQS queue that has no queue policy at all (verified). Real AWS drops them unless the queue policy lets sns.amazonaws.com SendMessage. The behavioural check (publish_reaches_both_queues) therefore passes for the naive solution on MiniStack; the static per-queue policy assertions are what catch it.

The policy assertions require an aws:SourceArn condition equal to the topic ARN (task spec). Real AWS would also deliver with a bare service-principal grant; requiring SourceArn is the confused-deputy best practice, so this is stricter than "would deliver". Principal "*" / {"AWS":"*"} restricted by aws:SourceArn (the older console-generated form) is accepted, since AWS delivers with it.
Seeded state was added beyond the task spec (an existing inventory-events -> inventory-q fan-out) so collateral damage is checked here as in the other brownfield tasks.
